A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ethical therapists are able to balance their own needs with those of the patient in a way that promotes the well-being of the patient and the profession.

the ethical therapist is one who is able to critically evaluate their own attitudes, beliefs, and behaviors in relation to their patients, who is open to the views of others, and who is able to reflect on and learn from experience.
the practice of psychotherapy is a complex and multifaceted activity.

the therapist must always be aware of his or her own ethical responsibilities, and be willing to take the time to reflect and consult when faced with an ethical dilemma.
the contemporary therapist must possess the capacity to engage in critical thinking and to be self-reflective.
